subject: math
title: Converting Units with Ratios
seo_title: Grade 6 Converting Units with Ratios Worksheets: Ratio Tables, Double Number Lines, Rates
standard_text: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets on converting units with ratios: use 1 ft : 12 in style conversion ratios, ratio tables and double number lines, fractions and decimals of units, inches to centimeters with 1 in = 2.54 cm, and converting rates like 60 miles per hour = 1 mile per minute. 100 practice questions with an answer key and step-by-step explanations.
key_big: A conversion fact is a ratio. Use equivalent ratios to convert.
key_sub: 1 ft : 12 in, so 5 ft : 60 in. To a smaller unit, multiply (5 yd = 15 ft). To a bigger unit, divide (48 oz = 3 lb). For a rate, convert both parts: 60 mi per hr = 1 mi per min.
body_html:
The big idea

Every conversion fact is a ratio. 1 ft = 12 in means the ratio of feet to inches is 1 : 12. Equivalent ratios give every other conversion: 2 : 24, 3 : 36, 5 : 60.

Multiply or divide?

To a smaller unit, you need more of them: multiply. To a bigger unit, you need fewer of them: divide.

Both ways

5 yd = ☐ ft   and   48 oz = ☐ lb

1 yd : 3 ft, so 5 × 3 = 15. 1 lb : 16 oz, so 48 ÷ 16 = 3.

Answer: 15 ft and 3 lb

Let the units cancel

Multiply by a fraction equal to 1, like 1 yd3 ft. Put the unit you want to remove on the bottom.

Feet to yards

9 ft = ☐ yd

9 ft × 1 yd3 ft = 9 ÷ 3 yd. The feet cancel.

Answer: 3 yd

Between systems

Use the rate you are given, such as 1 in = 2.54 cm or 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb (about).

Inches to centimeters

Use 1 in = 2.54 cm. 10 in = ☐ cm

A centimeter is smaller, so multiply: 10 × 2.54 = 25.4.

Answer: 25.4 cm

Converting a rate

A rate has two units. Change one part or both, one at a time.

Miles per hour

60 mi per hr = ☐ mi per min

1 hr = 60 min, so 60 miles in 60 minutes is 60 ÷ 60 = 1 mile each minute.

Answer: 1 mi per min

Price per ounce

$4.80 per lb = ☐ per oz

1 lb = 16 oz, so 1 ounce costs $4.80 ÷ 16 = $0.30.

Answer: $0.30 per oz

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying to get a bigger unit (6 ft = 18 yd)Bigger unit, fewer of them: 6 ft ÷ 3 = 2 yd
Using the wrong fact (1 yd = 12 in)1 yd = 3 ft = 36 in. 1 ft = 12 in
Mixing up capacity (1 gal = 2 qt)1 gal = 4 qt, 1 qt = 2 pt, 1 pt = 2 cups
Using 100 for kilo (1 km = 100 m)Kilo means 1,000: 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 kg = 1,000 g
Adding to both parts of a ratio (1 : 12 → 5 : 16)Multiply both parts: 1 : 12 → 5 : 60
Changing only one part of a rate90 km per hr: change km to m AND hours to minutes

faq.q: How do you use ratios to convert units in 6th grade?
faq.a: Write the conversion fact as a ratio, such as 1 ft : 12 in, then find an equivalent ratio with a ratio table, a double number line or multiplication: 5 ft : 60 in.

faq.q: How do you know whether to multiply or divide when converting units?
faq.a: To a smaller unit, multiply, because you need more of them (5 yd = 15 ft). To a bigger unit, divide, because you need fewer of them (48 oz = 3 lb).

faq.q: How do you convert 60 miles per hour to miles per minute?
faq.a: An hour has 60 minutes, so divide both numbers by 60: 60 miles per hour = 1 mile per minute.
It is the Common Core Grade 6 standard for using ratio reasoning to convert measurement units, including converting rates and handling units correctly when you multiply or divide.

sets.title: The conversion ratio: multiply or divide?

items.q: 1 foot is the same length as 12 inches. Which ratio shows this?
items.e: Write the units in the same order as the words: 1 foot to 12 inches is 1 ft : 12 in. (12 ft : 1 in turns it around, and 36 is the number of inches in a yard.)

items.q: Which ratio is correct for yards and feet?
items.e: 1 yard = 3 feet, so the ratio is 1 yd : 3 ft. (12 is inches in a foot, and 36 is inches in a yard, not feet.)

items.q: Which ratio is correct for gallons and quarts?
items.e: 1 gallon = 4 quarts, so the ratio is 1 gal : 4 qt. (2 is pints in a quart, and 8 is pints in a gallon.)

items.q: Which ratio is correct for kilometers and meters?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 km = 1,000 m and the ratio is 1 km : 1,000 m. (1 m = 100 cm, but 1 km is 1,000 m, not 100 m.)

items.q: Convert. 5 yd = ☐ ft
items.e: The ratio is 1 yd : 3 ft. Feet are smaller, so you need more of them: multiply by 3. 5 × 3 = 15, so 5 yd = 15 ft. (60 ft uses 12, the inches in a foot. 1 23 ft divides instead of multiplying, and 8 ft adds 3.)

items.q: To change 60 in to feet, what do you do?
items.e: The ratio is 1 ft : 12 in. A foot is bigger than an inch, so there will be fewer feet: divide by 12. 60 ÷ 12 = 5, so 60 in = 5 ft. (Dividing by 3 or 36 would give yards.)

items.q: Convert. 7 lb = ☐ oz
items.e: The ratio is 1 lb : 16 oz. Ounces are smaller, so you need more of them: multiply by 16. 7 × 16 = 112, so 7 lb = 112 oz. (84 oz uses 12 and 70 oz uses 10. 23 oz adds 16 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Convert. 6 qt = ☐ pt
items.e: The ratio is 1 qt : 2 pt. Pints are smaller, so you need more of them: multiply by 2. 6 × 2 = 12, so 6 qt = 12 pt. (3 pt divides instead of multiplying, 24 pt uses 4, the quarts in a gallon, and 8 pt adds 2.)

items.q: To change 9 gal to quarts, what do you do?
items.e: The ratio is 1 gal : 4 qt. A quart is smaller than a gallon, so there will be more quarts: multiply by 4. 9 × 4 = 36, so 9 gal = 36 qt. (1 qt = 2 pt and 1 gal = 8 pt, so 2 and 8 are for pints.)

items.q: Convert. 4 km = ☐ m
items.e: The ratio is 1 km : 1,000 m. Meters are smaller, so you need more of them: multiply by 1,000. 4 × 1,000 = 4,000, so 4 km = 4,000 m. (400 m uses 1 km = 100 m, and 0.004 m divides instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Convert. 48 oz = ☐ lb
items.e: The ratio is 1 lb : 16 oz. Pounds are bigger, so you need fewer of them: divide by 16. 48 ÷ 16 = 3, so 48 oz = 3 lb. (768 lb multiplies instead of dividing, 4 lb uses 12, and 4.8 lb uses 10.)

items.q: Convert. 20 qt = ☐ gal
items.e: The ratio is 1 gal : 4 qt. Gallons are bigger, so you need fewer of them: divide by 4. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so 20 qt = 5 gal. (80 gal multiplies instead of dividing, 10 gal uses 2, and 2 gal uses 10.)

items.q: Convert. 3,500 g = ☐ kg
items.e: The ratio is 1 kg : 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger, so you need fewer of them: divide by 1,000. 3,500 ÷ 1,000 = 3.5, so 3,500 g = 3.5 kg. (35 kg divides by 100, 0.35 kg divides by 10,000, and 3,500,000 kg multiplies instead of dividing.)

items.q: Convert. 180 min = ☐ hr
items.e: The ratio is 1 hr : 60 min. Hours are bigger, so you need fewer of them: divide by 60. 180 ÷ 60 = 3, so 180 min = 3 hr. (1.8 hr uses 100 minutes in an hour, 18 hr divides by 10, and 10,800 hr multiplies instead of dividing.)

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 1 ft : 12 in?
items.e: Multiply both parts of 1 ft : 12 in by 5: 5 ft : 60 in. (5 ft : 16 in adds 4 to both parts. Adding does not keep the ratio the same.)

items.q: Convert. 72 in = ☐ yd
items.e: The ratio is 1 yd : 36 in. Yards are bigger, so you need fewer of them: divide by 36. 72 ÷ 36 = 2, so 72 in = 2 yd. (6 is the number of feet, not yards. 24 yd divides by 3, the feet in a yard, and 2,592 yd multiplies instead of dividing.)

items.q: Convert. 2 mi = ☐ ft
items.e: The ratio is 1 mi : 5,280 ft. Feet are smaller, so you need more of them: multiply by 5,280. 2 × 5,280 = 10,560, so 2 mi = 10,560 ft. (2,640 ft divides instead of multiplying, 3,520 is the number of yards in 2 miles, and 10,000 ft uses 1 mi = 5,000 ft.)

items.q: To change 9 ft to yards, you multiply 9 ft by a fraction equal to 1. Which fraction?
items.e: Put feet on the bottom so the feet cancel and yards are left: 9 ft × (1 yd over 3 ft) = 9 ÷ 3 yd = 3 yd. The answer is 1 yd over 3 ft. (With 3 ft over 1 yd, the feet do not cancel.)

items.q: To change 5 gal to quarts, you multiply 5 gal by a fraction equal to 1. Which fraction?
items.e: Put gallons on the bottom so the gallons cancel and quarts are left: 5 gal × (4 qt over 1 gal) = 5 × 4 qt = 20 qt. The answer is 4 qt over 1 gal. (1 gal = 4 qt, not 2 or 8.)

items.q: Luis says 8 pt = 16 qt. What mistake did he make?
items.e: The ratio is 1 qt : 2 pt. A quart is bigger than a pint, so there are fewer quarts: 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so 8 pt = 4 qt. Luis multiplied 8 × 2 = 16. He multiplied instead of dividing.

sets.title: Ratio tables and double number lines

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 ft : 12 in, so each bottom number is 12 × the top number. 5 × 12 = 60. (48 is the next number in the pattern, but the table jumps from 3 to 5, not to 4.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 yd : 3 ft. Each step on the top line adds 1 yard, and each step on the bottom line adds 3 feet. 4 × 3 = 12. (48 uses 12, 144 uses 36, the inches in a yard, and 7 adds 3 to 4.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 gal : 4 qt, so each top number is the bottom number ÷ 4. 36 ÷ 4 = 9. (144 multiplies instead of dividing, 18 uses 2 quarts in a gallon, and 12 divides by 3.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 m : 100 cm, so 3 m = 3 × 100 = 300 cm. (30 uses 10 cm in a meter, 3,000 uses 1,000, and 103 adds instead of multiplying.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: Each tick is 2 ft = 24 in. 6 ft = 6 × 12 = 72 in. (60 uses 10 inches in a foot, 50 adds 2 to 48 as on the top line, and 18 uses 3.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 lb : 16 oz, so each top number is the bottom number ÷ 16. 128 ÷ 16 = 8. (6 is the next counting number, 2,048 multiplies, and 12.8 divides by 10.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 qt : 4 cups, so 12 cups ÷ 4 = 3 quarts. It lines up with 12 on the cups line. (6 uses 2 cups in a quart, 48 multiplies instead of dividing, and 12 is the number of cups, not quarts.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 hr : 60 min, so each top number is the bottom number ÷ 60. 300 ÷ 60 = 5. (3 uses 100 minutes in an hour, 30 divides by 10, and 18,000 multiplies.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 kg : 1,000 g, so 4,500 g ÷ 1,000 = 4.5 kg. (45 divides by 100, 0.45 divides by 10,000, and 4,500,000 multiplies.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 L : 1,000 mL, so 1.5 L = 1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500 mL. The ? is halfway between 1,000 and 2,000. (150 uses 100, 15,000 uses 10,000, and 1,050 reads 1.5 L as 1 L 50 mL.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 hr : 60 min, so 2.5 hr = 2.5 × 60 = 150 min. Each tick adds 30 minutes: 120 + 30 = 150. (250 uses 100 minutes in an hour, 125 uses 50, and 170 reads 2.5 hr as 2 hr 50 min.)

items.q: The table shows gallons and quarts. How many quarts are in 1 gallon?
items.e: Divide any bottom number by its top number: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 20 ÷ 5 = 4, 32 ÷ 8 = 4. So 1 gal = 4 qt. (9 subtracts 12 − 3. Ratios compare by dividing, not subtracting. 2 is the pints in a quart, and 12 qt is 3 gallons.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: First find the unit rate: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 inches for each foot. 10 × 12 = 120. (108 adds 36 again, but the top went up by 4, not 3. 100 uses 10, and 30 uses 3.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: Each quart is 2 pints, so each bottom number is the top number ÷ 2. 16 ÷ 2 = 8. (11 adds 6 because the top went up by 6, but adding does not keep the ratio. 32 multiplies, and 4 divides by 4.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 m : 100 cm, so each bottom number is the top number ÷ 100. 300 ÷ 100 = 3. (30 divides by 10, 0.3 divides by 1,000, and 30,000 multiplies.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: Unit rate: 72 ÷ 2 = 36 inches in each yard. 288 ÷ 36 = 8. (24 divides by 12, which gives feet, and 96 divides by 3.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 lb : 16 oz, so 1.5 lb = 1.5 × 16 = 24 oz (16 + 8). (21 reads 1.5 lb as 1 lb 5 oz, 15 uses 10, and 12 uses 8 ounces for each pound.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 lb : 16 oz, so each bottom number is the top number ÷ 16. 72 ÷ 16 = 4.5. (6 divides by 12, 7.2 divides by 10, and 1,152 multiplies.)

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 in = 2.54 cm, so each tick adds 2.54 cm. 3 × 2.54 = 7.62. (7.08 adds 2 instead of 2.54, 15.24 multiplies 5.08 by 3, and 1.18 divides 3 by 2.54.)

items.q: Convert. 2.5 gal = ☐ qt
items.e: The ratio is 1 gal : 4 qt, so multiply: 2.5 × 4 = 10 qt. (8 qt forgets the 0.5 gal, 5 qt uses 2, and 13 qt reads 2.5 gal as 2 gal 5 qt.)

items.q: Convert. 2 ft 8 in = ☐ in
items.e: 2 ft = 2 × 12 = 24 in. Add the 8 inches: 24 + 8 = 32 in. (28 in uses 10 inches in a foot, 10 in adds 2 + 8, and 24 in forgets the 8 inches.)

items.q: Convert. 0.75 L = ☐ mL
items.e: The ratio is 1 L : 1,000 mL, so multiply: 0.75 × 1,000 = 750 mL. (75 mL multiplies by 100, 7.5 mL by 10, and 7,500 mL by 10,000.)

items.q: Convert. 34 lb = ☐ oz
items.e: The ratio is 1 lb : 16 oz, so multiply: 34 × 16 = 484 = 12 oz. (7.5 oz uses 10, 21 13 oz divides 16 by 34, and 4 oz is only 14 lb.)

items.q: Convert. 42 in = ☐ ft
items.e: The ratio is 1 ft : 12 in, so divide: 42 ÷ 12 = 3 R6. 6 inches is 612 = 12 foot, so 42 in = 3 12 ft. (3.6 ft is a mistake for 3 ft 6 in, 4.2 ft divides by 10, and 504 ft multiplies.)

items.q: Convert. 3.2 km = ☐ m
items.e: The ratio is 1 km : 1,000 m, so multiply: 3.2 × 1,000 = 3,200 m. (320 m uses 100, 32,000 m uses 10,000, and 0.0032 m divides instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Convert. 2.5 lb = ☐ oz
items.e: The ratio is 1 lb : 16 oz, so multiply: 2.5 × 16 = 40 oz. (37 oz reads 2.5 lb as 2 lb 5 oz, 25 oz uses 10, and 32 oz forgets the 0.5 lb.)

items.q: Convert. 1.25 hr = ☐ min
items.e: The ratio is 1 hr : 60 min, so multiply: 1.25 × 60 = 75 min. (125 min uses 100 minutes in an hour, 85 min reads 1.25 hr as 1 hr 25 min, and 15 min forgets the whole hour.)

items.q: Convert. 30 oz = ☐ lb ☐ oz
items.e: 1 lb : 16 oz. 30 ÷ 16 = 1 R14: 1 whole pound and 14 ounces left over, so 30 oz = 1 lb 14 oz. (3 lb divides by 10, 1.14 lb writes the remainder as a decimal, and 2 lb 6 oz uses 12.)

items.q: Convert. 5 qt = ☐ gal
items.e: The ratio is 1 gal : 4 qt, so divide: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 R1. The extra quart is 14 gal, so 5 qt = 1 14 gal. (1.1 gal writes the remainder as a decimal, 20 gal multiplies, and 2 12 gal uses 2.)

items.q: Convert. 2 14 ft = ☐ in
items.e: The ratio is 1 ft : 12 in. 2 × 12 = 24, and 14 of 12 = 3, so 2 14 ft = 24 + 3 = 27 in. (24 in forgets the 14 ft, 28 in uses 14 ft = 4 in, and 22 12 in uses 10.)

items.q: Convert. 10 cups = ☐ qt
items.e: The ratio is 1 qt : 4 cups, so divide: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 R2. 2 cups is 24 = 12 qt, so 10 cups = 2 12 qt. (5 qt uses 2 cups in a quart, 40 qt multiplies, and 2.2 qt writes the remainder as a decimal.)

items.q: Convert. 3,750 mL = ☐ L
items.e: The ratio is 1 L : 1,000 mL, so divide: 3,750 ÷ 1,000 = 3.75 L. (37.5 L divides by 100, 0.375 L divides by 10,000, and 3,750,000 L multiplies.)

items.q: Convert. 1 12 mi = ☐ ft
items.e: The ratio is 1 mi : 5,280 ft. 1 mi = 5,280 ft and 12 mi = 2,640 ft, so 1 12 mi = 5,280 + 2,640 = 7,920 ft. (5,280 ft forgets the 12 mi, 2,640 ft is only the 12 mi, and 7,500 ft uses 1 mi = 5,000 ft.)

items.q: Convert. 1 34 hr = ☐ min
items.e: The ratio is 1 hr : 60 min. 1 hr = 60 min and 34 of 60 = 45 min, so 1 34 hr = 60 + 45 = 105 min. (175 min uses 100 minutes in an hour, 60 min forgets the 34 hr, and 75 min uses 14 hr instead of 34 hr.)

items.q: Convert. 1 gal 3 qt = ☐ cups
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt, so 1 gal 3 qt = 7 qt. The ratio is 1 qt : 4 cups, so 7 × 4 = 28 cups. (7 is the number of quarts, 14 is the number of pints, and 19 adds 16 cups + 3.)

items.q: Convert. 27 in = ☐ yd
items.e: The ratio is 1 yd : 36 in, so divide: 2736 = 34 yd. (2 14 divides by 12, which gives feet. 9 yd divides by 3, and 0.27 yd divides by 100.)

items.q: Convert. 4 ft 9 in = ☐ ft
items.e: 1 ft : 12 in, so 9 in = 912 = 34 ft. 4 ft 9 in = 4 34 ft. (4.9 ft treats 9 inches as 9 tenths of a foot, 57 is the number of inches, and 4 14 uses 936, a part of a yard.)

items.q: Which is the same length as 5 12 yd?
items.e: The ratio is 1 yd : 3 ft, so multiply: 5 × 3 = 15 and 12 × 3 = 1 12. 15 + 1 12 = 16 12 ft. (15 12 ft forgets to multiply the 12 by 3, 66 ft uses 12, and 1 56 ft divides.)

items.q: Which is NOT equal to 2.25 hr?
items.e: 0.25 hr = 14 hr = 14 of 60 = 15 min. So 2.25 hr = 2 14 hr = 2 hr 15 min = 135 min. 2 hr 25 min reads the .25 as 25 minutes, but an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

items.q: Use 1 in = 2.54 cm. Convert. 10 in = ☐ cm
items.e: The ratio is 1 in : 2.54 cm. A centimeter is smaller, so multiply: 10 × 2.54 = 25.4 cm. (3.94 divides instead of multiplying, 254 moves the point too far, and 12.54 adds 10 + 2.54.)

items.q: Use 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb. A bag of rice is 5 kg. About how many pounds is it?
items.e: A pound is smaller than a kilogram, so there are more pounds: multiply. 5 × 2.2 = 11, so 5 kg is about 11 lb. (2.3 divides, 7.2 adds 5 + 2.2, and 110 moves the point.)

items.q: Use 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km. About how many kilometers is 5 mi?
items.e: A kilometer is shorter than a mile, so there are more kilometers: 5 × 1.6 = about 8 km. (3.1 divides, 6.6 adds 5 + 1.6, and 80 moves the point.)

items.q: Use 1 gal ≈ 3.8 L. A fish tank holds 5 gal. About how many liters is that?
items.e: A liter is smaller than a gallon, so multiply: 5 × 3.8 = about 19 L. (1.3 divides, 8.8 adds 5 + 3.8, and 190 moves the point.)

items.q: 60 miles per hour is the same speed as how many miles per minute?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min, so 60 miles in 60 minutes is 60 ÷ 60 = 1 mile per minute. (60 mi per min forgets to change the hour, 3,600 multiplies instead of dividing, and 6 divides by 10.)

items.q: Use 1 in = 2.54 cm. A ruler is 12 in long. How long is it in centimeters?
items.e: Multiply by the ratio 2.54 cm for each inch: 12 × 2.54 = 30.48 cm. (4.72 divides instead of multiplying, 14.54 adds 12 + 2.54, and 304.8 puts the point in the wrong place.)

items.q: Use 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb. A dog weighs 44 lb. About how many kilograms is that?
items.e: A kilogram is bigger than a pound, so there are fewer kilograms: divide. 44 ÷ 2.2 = 20, so 44 lb is about 20 kg. (96.8 multiplies, 41.8 subtracts, and 2 divides 44 by 22.)

items.q: Use 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km. A race is 10 km long. About how many miles is that?
items.e: A mile is longer than a kilometer, so there are fewer miles: divide. 10 ÷ 1.6 = 6.25, so the race is about 6.25 mi. (16 multiplies, 8.4 subtracts, and 62.5 puts the point in the wrong place.)

items.q: Use 1 in = 2.54 cm. Convert. 127 cm = ☐ in
items.e: An inch is bigger than a centimeter, so there will be fewer inches: divide. 127 ÷ 2.54 = 50 in. (322.58 multiplies instead of dividing, 124.46 subtracts, and 5 divides by 25.4.)

items.q: To change 8 in to centimeters, you multiply 8 in by a fraction. Which fraction?
items.e: Put inches on the bottom so the inches cancel and centimeters are left: 8 in × (2.54 cm over 1 in) = 8 × 2.54 cm = 20.32 cm. The answer is 2.54 cm over 1 in.

items.q: A faucet fills 3 gal per minute. How many quarts per minute is that?
c: 34 qt per min
items.e: Change only the gallons: 1 gal : 4 qt, so 3 × 4 = 12 qt per minute. The time stays “per minute.” (34 divides, 6 uses 2, and 180 multiplies by 60, but the time does not change.)

items.q: A hose sprays 120 L per hour. How many liters per minute is that?
items.e: Change only the time: 1 hr = 60 min, so 120 ÷ 60 = 2 L per minute. (7,200 multiplies, 12 divides by 10, and 1.2 uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: Juice costs $2 per quart. At this rate, what is the price per gallon?
items.e: 1 gal = 4 qt, so a gallon costs 4 × $2 = $8.00. ($0.50 divides, $4.00 uses 2 quarts in a gallon, and $16.00 uses 8, the pints in a gallon.)

items.q: Cheese costs $4.80 per pound. What is the price per ounce?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz, so the price of 1 ounce is $4.80 ÷ 16 = $0.30. ($76.80 multiplies, $0.40 uses 12 ounces in a pound, and $0.48 uses 10.)

items.q: A cheetah can run 30 m per second. How many meters per minute is that?
items.e: 1 min = 60 sec, so in 1 minute it runs 30 × 60 = 1,800 m. (30 forgets to change the time, 0.5 divides, and 180 multiplies by 6.)

items.q: A pump moves 48 cups of water per minute. How many gallons per minute is that?
items.e: 1 gal = 16 cups, so 48 ÷ 16 = 3 gal per minute. (12 gives quarts, 6 uses 8, the pints in a gallon, and 768 multiplies.)

items.q: Rice costs $1.60 per kilogram. What do 500 g of rice cost?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 500 g = 0.5 kg. 0.5 × $1.60 = $0.80. ($800.00 forgets to convert, $8.00 uses 100 g in a kilogram, and $3.20 doubles instead of halving.)

items.q: A train travels 90 km per hour. How many meters per minute is that?
items.e: Change both parts. Distance: 90 km = 90,000 m. Time: 1 hr = 60 min. 90,000 ÷ 60 = 1,500 m per minute. (90,000 changes only the distance, 1.5 changes only the time, and 5,400,000 multiplies by 60 instead of dividing.)

items.q: A bike goes 5 m per second. How many kilometers per hour is that?
items.e: Change both parts. In 1 hour (3,600 sec) it goes 5 × 3,600 = 18,000 m. 18,000 m = 18 km, so 18 km per hour. (18,000 forgets to change meters to kilometers, and 0.3 and 300 multiply by 60 only once.)

items.q: A car goes 30 miles per hour. How many feet per second is that?
items.e: Change both parts. In 1 hour it goes 30 × 5,280 = 158,400 ft. 1 hr = 3,600 sec, so 158,400 ÷ 3,600 = 44 ft per second. (158,400 changes only the distance, 2,640 divides by 60 only once, and 0.5 changes only the time.)

items.q: A track is 400 m around. Zoe runs 6 laps. How many kilometers does she run?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 400 = 2,400 m. Step 2: 1 km : 1,000 m, so 2,400 ÷ 1,000 = 2.4 km. (2,400 km forgets to convert, 24 km uses 100 m in a kilometer, and 0.24 km uses 10,000.)

items.q: A water bottle holds 750 mL. Noah drinks 4 bottles a day. How many liters is that?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × 750 = 3,000 mL. Step 2: 1 L : 1,000 mL, so 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3 L. (3,000 L forgets to convert, 30 L divides by 100, and 0.3 L divides by 10,000.)

items.q: A garden needs 3 sides of fence. Each side is 12 ft long. The fence is sold by the yard. How many yards are needed?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 12 = 36 ft. Step 2: 1 yd : 3 ft, so 36 ÷ 3 = 12 yd. (36 yd forgets to convert, 108 multiplies, and 3 yd divides by 12.)

items.q: A cooler holds 2.5 gal of lemonade. How many 1-cup servings is that?
items.e: 1 gal = 16 cups, so 2.5 × 16 = 40 servings. (10 counts quarts, 20 counts pints, and 25 uses 10 cups in a gallon.)

items.q: A soup recipe for 4 people uses 3 cups of broth. Omar makes soup for 16 people. How many quarts of broth does he need?
items.e: Step 1: 16 people is 4 times as many, so 4 × 3 = 12 cups. Step 2: 1 qt : 4 cups, so 12 ÷ 4 = 3 qt. (12 qt forgets to convert, 6 qt uses 2 cups in a quart, and 48 qt multiplies.)

items.q: Leo has 5 yd of ribbon. Each bow uses 9 in. How many bows can he make?
items.e: Step 1: 1 yd : 36 in, so 5 yd = 5 × 36 = 180 in. Step 2: 180 ÷ 9 = 20 bows. (6 bows uses 12 inches in a yard, 1 bow divides 15 ft by 9 without changing to inches, and 45 multiplies 5 × 9.)

items.q: Punch is made with 1 12 qt of juice and 3 pt of sparkling water. How many cups of punch is that?
items.e: Change to cups. 1 qt = 4 cups, so 1 12 qt = 6 cups. 1 pt = 2 cups, so 3 pt = 6 cups. 6 + 6 = 12 cups. (4 12 adds without converting, 9 uses 2 cups in a quart, and 18 uses 4 cups in a pint.)

items.q: Each room needs 3 qt of paint. Owen paints 6 rooms. How many gallons of paint does he use?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 3 = 18 qt. Step 2: 1 gal : 4 qt, so 18 ÷ 4 = 4 R2 = 4 12 gal. (18 gal forgets to convert, 9 gal uses 2, and 4.2 writes the remainder 2 as a decimal.)

items.q: A 2 L jug of juice is poured into glasses that hold 250 mL each. How many glasses can be filled?
items.e: Step 1: 1 L : 1,000 mL, so 2 L = 2,000 mL. Step 2: 2,000 ÷ 250 = 8 glasses. (4 uses only 1 L, 125 divides 250 by 2, and 500 multiplies.)

items.q: Grapes cost $2.40 per pound. Ruby buys 24 oz of grapes. How much does she pay?
items.e: Step 1: 1 lb : 16 oz, so 24 oz = 24 ÷ 16 = 1.5 lb. Step 2: 1.5 × $2.40 = $3.60. ($57.60 forgets to convert, $5.76 uses 24 oz = 2.4 lb, and $4.80 uses 12 ounces in a pound.)

items.q: A race is 5 km long. A track is 400 m around. How many laps of the track is the race?
items.e: Step 1: 5 km = 5 × 1,000 = 5,000 m. Step 2: 5,000 ÷ 400 = 12 12 laps. (1 14 uses 100 m in a kilometer, 80 divides 400 by 5, and 125 uses 10,000 m.)

items.q: Grace has 3 12 yd of rope. She cuts off 4 pieces that are each 2 ft long. How many feet of rope are left?
items.e: Step 1: 1 yd : 3 ft, so 3 12 yd = 10 12 ft. Step 2: 4 × 2 = 8 ft cut off. Step 3: 10 12 − 8 = 2 12 ft. (1 ft forgets the 12 yd, 34 ft uses 12, and 10 12 ft forgets to subtract.)

items.q: A pancake recipe uses 34 cup of milk for each batch. Sam has 1 qt of milk. How many full batches can he make?
items.e: Step 1: 1 qt = 4 cups. Step 2: 4 ÷ 34 = 4 × 43 = 163 = 5 13, so 5 full batches. (6 rounds up, but there is not enough milk for a 6th batch. 1 batch forgets to change quarts to cups, and 3 multiplies 4 × 34.)

items.q: Eli walks 4 miles per hour. How many feet does he walk in 15 minutes?
items.e: Step 1: 15 min = 14 hr, so he walks 4 × 14 = 1 mi. Step 2: 1 mi = 5,280 ft. (21,120 ft is a whole hour, 1,320 ft is only 14 mi, and 316,800 ft multiplies by 15 instead of taking 14.)

items.q: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. At the same rate, how far does it go in 40 minutes?
items.e: Step 1: unit rate: 180 ÷ 3 = 60 mi per hour = 1 mi per minute. Step 2: 40 × 1 = 40 mi. (24 uses 40 min = 0.4 hr, 2,400 multiplies 60 × 40, and 1 12 divides 60 by 40.)

items.q: Fabric costs $6 per meter. Emma needs 6 pieces that are each 75 cm long. How much does the fabric cost?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 75 = 450 cm. Step 2: 1 m : 100 cm, so 450 cm = 4.5 m. Step 3: 4.5 × $6 = $27.00. ($2,700 forgets to convert, $270 uses 10 cm in a meter, and $4.50 is the cost of only 1 piece.)

items.q: A pool holds 9,000 gal. A hose fills it at 15 gal per minute. How many hours does it take to fill?
items.e: Step 1: 9,000 ÷ 15 = 600 min. Step 2: 1 hr : 60 min, so 600 ÷ 60 = 10 hr. (600 forgets to change minutes to hours, 6 uses 100 minutes in an hour, and 135,000 multiplies.)

items.q: A puppy weighed 7 lb 8 oz. It gained 6 oz a week for 8 weeks. How much does it weigh now, in pounds?
items.e: Step 1: 8 × 6 = 48 oz gained. 48 ÷ 16 = 3 lb. Step 2: 7 lb 8 oz = 7 12 lb, and 7 12 + 3 = 10 12 lb. (10.8 lb is a mistake for 10 lb 8 oz, 13 12 lb uses 8 oz in a pound, and 55 12 adds 48 oz as pounds.)

items.q: Maya drinks 2 12 L of water every day from 500 mL bottles. How many bottles does she drink in a week?
items.e: Step 1: 2 12 L = 2,500 mL, and 2,500 ÷ 500 = 5 bottles a day. Step 2: 7 × 5 = 35 bottles. (5 is only one day, 3 12 uses 1 L = 100 mL, and 17 12 multiplies 2 12 × 7 without converting.)

items.q: Sofia runs 14 mi in 2 minutes. What is her speed in feet per second?
items.e: Change both parts. Distance: 14 mi = 5,280 ÷ 4 = 1,320 ft. Time: 2 min = 120 sec. 1,320 ÷ 120 = 11 ft per second. (22 divides by 60 and forgets that it took 2 minutes, 660 is feet per minute, and 1,320 is the whole distance, not the speed.)
